candidates.summary: isCrossingCurParam tests neither the declared type nor the first parameter's name, so a non-realm `cur` in a crossing function is refused as the frame identity
candidates.failure_scenario: The base gated all three write rules on the resolved type (`evalStaticTypeOf(store, last, ne) == gRealmType` at 2890 and 3116, `xt == gRealmType` at 2584). Head replaced that with isCrossingCurParam, which checks the name and the declaring node only. A crossing function's first realm parameter may be blank or unnamed (preprocess.go:2828 admits a `.arg` prefix), so any other `cur` it declares resolves to a crossing FuncDecl/FuncLitExpr. `func F(_ realm, cur int) int { cur = cur + 1; return cur }` compiles on b7845fb2d and is refused at 6d88deba7 with "cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter: it names the realm this frame is executing as"; `p := &cur` on the same int parameter is refused with "cannot take the address of a realm-typed `cur` ... `realm` is an interface, so a *realm is never needed", both false of an int. Same for a crossing function literal with a `cur string` parameter. `func F(_ realm, ...)` is idiomatic in the tree (r/gnoland/blog/admin.gno:26-109, r/gnoland/boards2/v0/public.gno:118), so the precondition is ordinary; no fixture covers the shape, so no CI job reaches it. The PR body's Compatibility paragraph, "No .gno source that compiled and ran before is rejected now: the write rules only got narrower", is false in this direction.
candidates.verify_by: cp the two artifacts into gnovm/tests/files/ and run `go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles/PROBE.gno$' -v` at 6d88deba7 and at b7845fb2d; head FAILs both, base PASSes both. Adding `&& ft.Params[0].Name == "cur"` to both arms, or restoring the gRealmType test, clears it.

candidates.failure_scenario: `func namedResult(x int) (cur realm)` is not crossing (first parameter is int), so isCrossingCurParam falls through its switch on any declarer test. The file's header claims "Only the parameter is fixed", which is false for a crossing function whose first realm parameter is blank or unnamed: `func F(_ realm) (cur realm) { cur = nil; return cur }` is refused with "cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter" at 6d88deba7. It is refused on b7845fb2d too, so the diff does not cause it; the diff sweeps this class ("The write rules refused more than the parameter") and misses this member, and the fixture that certifies the sweep is the one that does not cover it.

candidates.summary: the positive control passes nil into every realm slot, so it shows the write rules silent and never that the shapes carry a realm
candidates.failure_scenario: main is non-crossing, so no realm value exists in the file: setPkgCur(0, nil), namedResult(0) and rangeLocal(0, nil) exercise the three bindings with nil only. Threading a real realm into them is refused one level up, at the declaration: `func namedResult(r realm) (cur realm)` panics with "a crossing function's first realm argument must have name `cur`" (preprocess.go:2828), and a package-level realm var holding a non-nil realm panics at finalize ("cannot persist realm value", pinned by zrealm_cur_persist_var.gno). Saying so in the header is what stops the next reader from taking the file as proof these bindings are usable.
